products.name: Blackseed Oil
products.subtitle: Cold-pressed Nigella sativa seed oil
products.tagline: The original. One seed, one ingredient, one certificate per lot.
products.intendedUse: A daily spoonful of seed oil, taken straight or stirred into food.
products.sensory: Bold, peppery, a little bitter. Deep amber-gold. A big herbal aroma. This is an unrefined seed oil, not a neutral one.
products.storage: Cool, dark place. Refrigerate after opening.
directions: Shake gently. The oil is unfiltered and may show natural sediment.
Take one dropper, about 1 mL, with or after a meal.
Never heat it. Stir into food after cooking, not during.
howTo: One dropper, with or after a meal. Let it sit on the tongue a moment before swallowing.
Stir into honey, yogurt, or a smoothie, or drizzle over salad, labneh, or warm bread. Never heat it.
products.short: Single-ingredient Nigella sativa seed oil, cold pressed and bottled in amber glass. Every lot ships with a published laboratory certificate.
products.long: Most blackseed oil is sold on folklore. Ours is sold on a certificate. Each lot is pressed cold from one harvest, bottled unrefined and unblended, and released only after an independent laboratory has reported thymoquinone, fatty-acid profile, freshness, heavy metals, and a microbial screen. The number on your bottle’s lot page is that laboratory’s, not ours.
products.ingredients: Nigella sativa (black seed) oil.
specs: Single harvest per lot, named on the lot certificate
Amber glass, glass dropper, tamper-evident seal

c: Shake gently. The oil is unfiltered and may show natural sediment.
Take one dropper, about 1 mL, with or after a meal.
Never heat it. Stir into food after cooking, not during.
Why publish a certificate for every lot?

Because thymoquinone and freshness vary with the harvest and the press. A single number printed once on a label would be a marketing decision. A certificate per lot is a laboratory result, and it is the only number we will show you.
Does it taste strong?
Yes. Honest blackseed oil is peppery, slightly bitter, and aromatic. A bland oil has usually been refined, diluted, or stored too long.
Which size should I start with?
The 125 mL bottle is about four months at one dropper a day. The 250 and 500 mL sizes are priced lower per millilitre for households and practitioners.

c.safety: For adults. Read the full label. Talk to your clinician first if pregnant, nursing, taking medication, or managing a health condition. Discontinue and seek advice if any adverse reaction occurs.

Drizzle over rice, yogurt, or warm milk after cooking. Never heat it.
products.short: Hand-picked saffron infused for forty days in our lot-tested blackseed oil. A spoon in warm milk, over rice, or straight.
products.long: Saffron and black seed have shared the same kitchen shelf for a thousand years. We steep whole threads, never powder, in cold-pressed blackseed oil for forty days in the dark, then decant. The result is a deep gold oil with the honeyed, hay-and-leather aroma of real saffron and the peppery base of the seed.

c: Shake. Take one teaspoon daily, straight or stirred into warm milk or tea.
Finish rice, dal, or roasted vegetables with a thread of it.
Store sealed in a cool cupboard; use within four months of opening.
Why infuse instead of blend?
Saffron’s aroma compounds are oil-soluble but fragile. A slow, cold infusion carries them intact; blending powdered saffron does not.
Is the saffron graded?
Yes. We buy ISO 3632 Grade I threads and keep the supplier’s crocin and safranal assay on file with each lot.

c.safety: Food product. Contains no major allergens. Not for use in pregnancy without consulting your clinician. Natural sediment is normal.

why: Caffeine and rose hydrosol: a cooling, refreshed feel on application; rose water replaces fragrance so the formula stays fragrance-free near the eyes.
Niacinamide 4%: vitamin B3, one of the best-studied cosmetic ingredients. In published trials it improved the look of uneven tone and fine lines and helped skin feel more resilient.

Saffron: Crocus sativus stigma, the botanical behind Golden Hour and the Radiance oil, used in traditional cosmetics for a brighter-looking complexion; here it is carried in a light gel for the same brighter look under the eyes.
Blackseed: cold-pressed Nigella sativa, the constant across every product. Fatty acids that leave the skin’s moisture barrier feeling comfortable, so thin under-eye skin feels hydrated for longer.
Grapevine: Vitis vinifera shoot, the same botanical as the Renewal Serum. Polyphenols from the vine help even the appearance of skin tone and support a smoother-looking surface.

Stilbenes are the family of plant compounds that includes resveratrol and viniferins. Grapevine shoots contain far more than the grape itself, which is why we use the shoot.

Habit, mostly: the serum pairs well with the heavier face oil at night and leaves the morning routine shorter.

Grapevine shoot: standardized stilbenes, the family that includes resveratrol and viniferins, for skin that looks smoother and more even in tone.
